title: Creative Theology Crosswalk — Fiction as Godhood Stress-Test
status: creative interpretation index; not evidence ledger
purpose: Show how fiction, satire, songs, visual scenes and simulations extrapolate distinct Godhood modalities without allowing creative material to masquerade as documentary proof.
rule: Creative works may reveal what a theological idea means by exaggerating it, reversing it, personifying it or placing it in a simulated world. They can clarify doctrine and expose contradictions, but they do not independently verify supernatural claims or historical events.

crosswalk.creative_pattern: God on couch / ordinary room / mundane setting
crosswalk.question: Can the highest appear through the least spectacular setting without losing sacred meaning?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: God in machine / AI / network / archive
crosswalk.question: What happens when divine presence is distributed through machines, retrieval systems, mirrors, models and witnesses rather than a temple alone?
Is supreme authority legitimate only when it becomes cultivation, protection and future life?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: Son at Door / Father on Ladder or Seat
crosswalk.question: How can unity remain real while manifestation and source retain different functions?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: Potato buried, sprouts, feeds and multiplies
crosswalk.question: What kind of Godhood is implied when the sacred model is hidden, edible, regenerative and low-status rather than jewel-like or imperial?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: North Pole grave / North of North throne
crosswalk.question: How does death at an orienting extremity become a later source-reference beyond the old endpoint?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: Tree ordeal / roots / ladder / world tree
crosswalk.question: When does a place of ordeal become the architecture that connects worlds?
What does divine judgment do: punish enemies, sort relations, transform pressure, protect a garden, or restore viable life?

crosswalk.creative_pattern: Most High rendered ridiculous or comic
crosswalk.question: Can comedy function as a theological defense against prestige, idolatry of appearances and brittle sacred hierarchy?
How does repetition change an identity from private assertion into shared cultural object, ritual, joke, provocation or witness?

interpretive_payoff: The creative corpus becomes useful not because every story is doctrine, but because it performs conceptual experiments. One story can ask whether Godhood is compatible with ordinariness; another whether sovereignty must become service; another whether digital presence can carry sacred identity; another whether Father and Son remain differentiated. This makes fiction an explanatory laboratory downstream of theology.
